topic: The Great Depression and New Deal

question.leadin: One theory suggests that this woman and Fred Noonan died in the Mariana Islands while in Japanese custody.
question.text: Name this female aviator who left New Guinea aboard her plane, the Electra, but never arrived at Howland Island, which has spawned many theories about her disappearance.
question.clue: In July 2017 National Geographic sent border collies to a Kiribati island to investigate this person, while the History Channel claimed she was captured by the Japanese.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the political career of Franklin D. Roosevelt.
swap.text: In 1932, FDR defeated this man to become president. This president's administration oversaw the beginning of the Great Depression, for which he was widely unpopular.
swap.clue: Near the end of his term, he sent Douglas MacArthur to clear out the Bonus Army that was protesting for relief from the Great Depression.

question.text: This 31 st president was largely blamed for the Great Depression, and disgruntled citizens set up makeshift shantytowns sarcastically nicknamed after him.
question.clue: This man led the Food Administration during World War I, and MacArthur disobeyed his command to not attack the Bonus Army.

swap.leadin: Name some organizations established during the New Deal.
swap.text: This largest New Deal agency was created by the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935 and provided jobs and income to the unemployed; it also operated large arts, media, and literacy projects.
swap.clue: One branch of this organization was led by Hallie Flanagan, under whose leadership that branch undertook news reenactments called the "Living Newspaper," series, while another branch of this organization was responsible for producing the American Guide Series.

question.text: Capone first came to national attention after this 1929 event. During it, his Outfit shot seven rival gang members at ten o'clock in the morning in a parking garage.
question.clue: The victims of this event had been tricked into believing that they were waiting for a delivery of stolen whiskey.

swap.text: Perhaps the original photo of children in crisis is this one taken by Dorothea Lange showing two children turning to their mother for comfort in a California pea pickers' camp during the Great Depression.
swap.clue: Along with pictures at Japanese relocation camps, Dorothea Lange is also took this picture of Florence Owens Thompson during the Great Depression.

question.leadin: Name these things about U.S. foreign policy.
question.text: To emphasize cooperation and trade rather than military force in Central and South America, FDR established this policy in his 1933 inaugural address.
question.clue: This policy during the FDR administration in which the U.S. attempted to mend its relations with Latin America. Instead of interfering in other countries' affairs, the U.S. would act like the namesake of this policy.

swap.leadin: Name some things about colorful dogs in American history.
swap.text: Yellow-dog contracts were banned by this 1932 law. This law was sponsored by a Nebraska Senator who founded the Tennessee Valley Authority and a future New York City mayor who now names an airport in Queens.
swap.clue: The ruling in New Negro Alliance v. Sanitary Grocery Company applied this act to say federal courts could not prevent picketing.

question.leadin: Identify the following about some so-called "armies" from American history.
question.text: In 1932, these thousands of World War I veterans, led by Walter Waters, descended on Washington to demand payment for their wartime service.
question.clue: It protested a bill that was proposed by Wright Patman by embarking on a "death march" to Capitol Hill.

swap.leadin: The first of these explained the banking crisis and ended with the rallying cry "Together we cannot fail."
swap.text: Name this series of radio addresses delivered by Franklin Roosevelt.
swap.clue: Similar speeches were given while their speaker was Governor of New York.

question.text: The one and only North Dakotan ever to run for President, this candidate of Father Coughlin's Union Party polled 900,000 votes in the 1936 election after being drafted as a last-minute replacement for the assassinated Huey Long.
question.clue: After Long died, the Union Party ran this North Dakotan for President in 1936. He sponsored a mortgage refinancing act for farmers along with Lynn Frazier.

swap.leadin: One cause of this event decreased crop yields in Russia due to the Russian Revolution, which led to overcultivation of crops in the United States.
swap.text: Name this environmental disaster in the Midwest that occurred about the same time as the Great Depression, which caused the mass migration of thousands of "Okies."
swap.clue: This event saw numerous storms referred to as black blizzards.

question.text: This supervisor of the WPA was one of Roosevelt's closest advisors and served as Secretary of Commerce for Roosevelt near the end of his second term. He served as FDR's primary emissary to Britain during WWII and oversaw the lend lease program.
question.clue: The phrase "Arsenal of Democracy" was suggested by this advisor to FDR, who crafted the WPA and was integral in implementing the Lend Lease Program.

swap.leadin: Journalist Dainis Ivans ("dye-niss EE-vons") rose to popularity, and eventually became the first leader of Tautas Fronte, after successfully opposing a proposed structure of this type.
swap.text: Name these structures. The illicit trade of caviar in Russia increased when sturgeon populations decreased after the building of one of these structures on the Volga River.
swap.clue: Argentina briefly opposed the building of one of these structures, named Itaipu, between Paraguay and Brazil on the Paran´a River.

question.leadin: Norman Lear attributed his life of activism to stumbling across this man's antisemitic radio broadcasts as a boy.
question.text: Name this "Radio Priest" who reached a peak of 30 million Americans in the 1930s. He opposed both free markets and communism from his base in the Detroit suburb of Royal Oak.
question.clue: 1926 saw the debut of this Michigan-based Catholic preacher's popular radio show. He later went nuts and began advocating fascism on his broadcasts, and like a certain longwinded female quiz bowl player from the University of Ottawa, he was a vocal, Canadian-born anti-Semite.

swap.leadin: The Chicago Tribune compared this man to Rasputin.
swap.text: Name this adviser to Franklin Roosevelt. Besides being a diplomatic troubleshooter, he helped lead the Works Progress Administration and was Secretary of Commerce from late 1938 to 1940.

question.text: As chair of Louisiana's Public Interest Commission, Long established a populist brand by suing a company in this industry for a rebate of its 20% rate hike. Elisha Gray was a pioneer in this industry.
question.answerHtml: telephone industry [or telegraph industry, or telecommunications industry; accept Cumberland Telephone and Telegraph Company]

swap.leadin: While its first chairman was Peter Norbeck, this group was named for its fourth chief counsel, who would later become a commissioner of the SEC.
swap.text: Name this commission which was established to explore the causes of the Wall Street Crash of 1929.
swap.clue: Among the sections in the 400-page report produced by this investigative body were ones on "Manipulative devices," and "Abuse of proxies," as well as a chapter dedicated to investigating "Income-tax Avoidances."

question.leadin: Tom McCoy was a principal actor in this event, which in the span of a single day used the favorable results of a recount to reorganize the entire government of Rhode Island.
question.text: Identify this pivotal event of Rhode Island history which took place on January 1, 1935, and in which a possible case of voter fraud allowed Democrats to assume complete control of state politics.

swap.leadin: Name some details of Great Depression-era photographs.
swap.text: A portrait of Allie May Burroughs was taken in by this photographer, who documented rural Alabama through staying with the Burroughs, Fields, and Tingle families. He compiled his photos into the collection Let Us Now Praise Famous Men.
swap.clue: This photographer took pictures for the Farm Security Administration, documenting the Great Depression in Southern states, particularly Alabama. He collaborated with James Agee on Let Us Now Praise Famous Men.
